q: In an ecosystem, green plants that photosynthesise to produce food are called ______.
e: In an ecosystem, green plants that photosynthesise to produce food are called producers. Producers, mainly green plants, convert light to chemical energy. An ecosystem is a community plus its physical environment, linked by energy and materials. Decomposers is different: decomposers such as bacteria and fungi break down dead material and recycle nutrients.

q: Animals that eat plants or other animals are known as ______.
e: Animals that eat plants or other animals are known as consumers. Consumers get energy by eating other organisms. Reducers is not consumers.

q: Organisms that break down dead material and help to recycle nutrients are called ______.
e: Organisms that break down dead material and help to recycle nutrients are called decomposers. Decomposers such as bacteria and fungi break down dead material and recycle nutrients. An extra chromosome 21 produces Down's syndrome. Herbivores is not decomposers.

q: Abiotic factors include all of the following EXCEPT ______.
e: Abiotic factors include all of the following EXCEPT predation. Predation is one biotic interaction that structures communities. Abiotic factors are the non-living parts of the environment. Temperature is not predation.

q: Biotic factors include all of the following EXCEPT ______.
e: Biotic factors include all of the following EXCEPT salinity. Biotic factors are the living parts of the environment. Competition for food is not salinity.

q: All the organisms of a particular species found in an ecosystem at a certain time form a ______.
e: All the organisms of a particular species found in an ecosystem at a certain time form a population. A population is all the individuals of one species in an area. An ecosystem is a community plus its physical environment, linked by energy and materials. Habitat is different: a habitat is the place where an organism lives.

q: The populations of all species found in an ecosystem at a particular time form the ______.
e: The populations of all species found in an ecosystem at a particular time form the community. A community is all the populations living together in an area. An ecosystem is a community plus its physical environment, linked by energy and materials. Ecosphere is different: the ecosphere is hydrosphere, lithosphere, atmosphere, and biosphere together.

q: In a food chain, the arrow (→) means ______.
e: In a food chain, the arrow (→) means is eaten by. A food chain is one linear feeding path from producer onward. Competes with is not is eaten by.

q: The different stages in a food chain (producer, primary consumer, secondary consumer) are called ______.
e: The different stages in a food chain (producer, primary consumer, secondary consumer) are called trophic levels. Trophic levels are feeding steps in a food chain. A food chain is one linear feeding path from producer onward. Feeding zones is not trophic levels.

q: A food web shows feeding relationships with ______.
e: A food web shows feeding relationships with different food chains. Agriculture and husbandry both serve food production, but they are different practices. A food web is the network of linked food chains in a community. Only decomposers is not different food chains.
